title: Sync-R1: Bridging Understanding and Generation for Personalized Reasoning via Co-operative Reinforcement Learning
claim: Our method yields more faithful personalized understanding and generation than baselines, including on dense-text and reasoning-heavy prompts.
layout: 3 columns, baseline row above ours row, with per-attribute judging smileys
description: A two-row gallery with a baseline row on top (UniCTokens, Show-o) and Sync-R1 on the bottom. Each row has three groups. (1) Personalized MMU: chat dialogues about a user's cat <mam>, where the baseline gives a generic answer and Sync-R1 gives a detailed, personalized recommendation. (2) Concept to personalize: a green panel with a cat photo and text listing the concept's attributes. (3) Personalized T2I: prompts with highlighted keywords (red bow, fireplace, trees, gifts), the generated cat images, and a 'Judging' checklist of smiley faces. Baseline images miss attributes such as the fireplace and the red bow, while Sync-R1 images include them. Colored backgrounds separate the rows: gray for baselines, blue for ours.
caption: Capability Overview of Sync-R1. Our framework jointly optimizes personalized understanding and generation within a unified reasoning trajectory via Sync-GRPO. By establishing an explicit synergistic loop, Sync-R1 leverages the reciprocal enhancement between comprehension and creation to achieve precise integration of personalized concepts. Beyond standard personalization, Sync-R1 excels in challenging scenarios, including dense-text and reasoning-based generation tasks with missing concept information.
abstract: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) excel in general tasks but struggle to bridge the gap between personalized understanding and generation. Prior works largely rely on implicit token-level alignment via supervised fine-tuning, which fails to fully capture the potential synergy between comprehension and creation. In this work, we propose Sync-R1, an end-to-end reinforcement learning framework that jointly optimizes personalized understanding and generation within a single, explicit reasoning loop. Through this unified feedback process, Sync-R1 enables personalized comprehension to guide content creation, while the resulting generation quality reciprocally refines understanding within an integrated reward landscape. To efficiently orchestrate this dual-task synergy, we introduce Sync-GRPO, a reinforcement learning method utilizing an ensemble reward system. Furthermore, we propose Dynamic Group Scaling (DGS), which adaptively filters low-potential trajectories to reduce gradient variance and accelerate convergence. To better reflect real-world complexity, we introduce UnifyBench++, featuring denser textual descriptions and richer user contexts. Experimental results demonstrate that Sync-R1 achieves state-of-the-art performance, showcasing superior cross-task reasoning and robust personalization without requiring complex cold-start procedures. The code and the UnifyBench++ dataset will be released at: https://github.com/arctanxarc/UniCTokens.
